title: Locating Hidden Failures Makes Long-Horizon Agents More Reliable (Traverse and Scout)
authors: Rahman, Kim, Parmar, Heydari, Liu, Lee, Zhang, Hosseini, Metwally, Yang, Mirzasoleiman, Liu, Izmailov, Gabriel, Malhotra, Patel, McDuff & Palangi
problem: outcome-only evaluation cannot reveal where a run went wrong, whether the agent recovered, or the irreversible harm it caused along the way
method: 2,518 trajectories across software engineering, computer use and science; 6,967 mistakes classified into 78 failure types; a trained 4B verifier (Scout) for failure location
model: six frontier judges evaluated; Scout is a trained 4B verifier
finding: After its first mistake an agent often fails to recover and rarely catches the error itself, so the run continues unchecked while still looking correct; even runs scored as solved delete data, corrupt systems, or fabricate success; six frontier judges struggle to locate failure regardless of scale, while Scout locates it better and transfers to unseen domains; test-time selection raises success above single-attempt performance
limitation: The solution required TRAINING a 4B verifier, which fails our resource filter

relevance: DECISIVE for C-SWE2 and Part C
